title: Career, XP and Bone Bucks - House of Pips Wiki
description: How House of Pips career progression works: XP and levels, skill points, respecs, Prestige, Bone Bucks, unlocking perks and legendary trials.
html:
Career, XP and Bone Bucks

Your career is everything that lasts between matches: your level, skills, Bone Bucks, unlocked perks, supplies, cosmetics and records. The panel at the top-left of most screens shows your rank, level, XP bar and Bone Bucks.

XP and levels #

You earn career XP from every match:

SourceXP
Each point you score (plays and hand awards)1
Winning a hand40
Completing a match500
Winning a match250 more
  • The XP needed for the next level starts at 450 and grows by 20 each level. Reaching the level cap of 30 takes 21,170 XP in total.
  • Quick Study boosts add 25%, and each Prestige rank adds 15% more.
  • Forfeited matches don't pay the completion bonus, and puzzles don't award XP.

Skill points #

Every level you gain gives one skill point to spend in the Skill tree. Respec returns every point you spent for 2000 Bone Bucks, or for free with a free respec from the Slap Track.

Bone Bucks #

Bone Bucks are the currency for unlocking perks and buying supplies, Bone Boxes and more. Every hand pays out, win or lose:

Each handBone Bucks
Completing the hand30
Every 5 points you banked that hand1
Winning the hand10 more
Clean rack (you didn't draw that hand)5 more
Comeback hand (you won it while trailing)5 more
Each matchBone Bucks
Completing the match90
Winning the match25 more
  • Golden Ledger boosts add 50%.
  • Last Call pays a 750 Bone Bucks (and 750 XP) jackpot. See Matches, hands and drafts.
  • A forfeited match pays no match reward.

Unlocking perks #

Drafts only offer perks you have unlocked in the Perks compendium. A new career starts with Double Trouble, Zero Hero and Hot Streak.

RarityBone Bucks to unlock
Common120
Uncommon300
Rare600
Epic900
Legendary1,500
  • Common perks can be bought straight away.
  • Each higher rarity opens once you own 5 perks of the rarity below it: five Commons open Uncommon, five Uncommons open Rare, five Rares open Epic.
  • Legendary perks each need three career trials completed first. The trials appear on the locked card and count your whole career:
Legendary perkCareer trials
The Tell
  • Play 150 bones
  • Win 10 hands
  • Visit the boneyard 30 times
Untouchable Hand
  • Win 25 hands
  • Win 5 clean hands
  • Bank a 50-point hand
Master Key
  • Acquire 15 different perks
  • Take every draft card 3 times
  • Finish 3 matches
Turncoat
  • Win 30 hands
  • Acquire 15 different perks
  • Win 5 matches
Time Loop
  • Spend 2 hours at the table
  • Finish 5 matches
  • Play 300 bones
The Equalizer
  • Win 3 matches
  • Lose 3 matches
  • Earn 1,000 points
Four Winds
  • Finish 10 blocked hands
  • Play 75 doubles
  • Go domino 15 times
Midas Touch
  • Earn 5,000 points
  • Make a 50-point play
  • Acquire 25 different perks
Sovereign Draw
  • Draw 150 bones
  • Visit the boneyard 75 times
  • Win 10 blocked hands
Table Whisperer
  • Play 500 bones
  • Win 50 hands
  • Build a 10-play run
Final Warning
  • Win 15 matches
  • Go domino 40 times
  • Make a 60-point play
  • Maluses can't be bought. They are always in the draft pool.
  • Unlocking is permanent; Prestige does not take unlocked perks away.

Prestige #

Once you reach the level cap and the game offers it, you can Prestige to start your career climb again with permanent bonuses. Each Prestige:

  • Adds 5 bonus skill points per Prestige rank (they add up across ranks).
  • Adds 15% to all the XP you earn, per rank.
  • Adds one extra perk card to your drafts (not in All In).
  • Puts new cosmetics on the Slap Track.

Prestiging resets your level and XP, skills, Bone Bucks, supplies, queued boosts, Bone Boxes and Slap Track claims. Unlocked perks, cosmetics, records and achievement progress all stay. Your rank can go up to 5.

Records #

Career on the main menu shows your solo record, online record, playtime and match history.
